correctness.rationale: Munn-tree walks from shifted roots have exact optimal cost 2E-distance. The cited conjugacy criterion ensures the admissible pairs are exactly the conjugates. First occurrence and endpoint equality in free groups compute E in deterministic L; edge-crossing parity computes pair distances in deterministic L, and pair maximization uses only logarithmic counters. Explicit finite independent enumerations up to length 6 support but do not prove the unbounded theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2026 geometric root-shift and optimality criteria imply the 2E-M expression; this formula is acknowledged as prior. The new, separately supported assertion is that E and M can be evaluated deterministically in logarithmic work space using first-occurrence edge enumeration and parity, and hence ConjGeo belongs to L. Primary literature and published-record semantic searches did not yield a directly stronger coverage statement. The remaining risk is a previously unindexed equivalent algorithm.
residual_risks: A separately indexed or unpublished equivalent deterministic logspace conjugacy-geodesic algorithm may predate this theorem.
The explicit geometric 2E-M minimum is implied by Carvalho–Monteiro (2026); only algorithmic space bound is asserted new.
The verifier exhausts a finite input range, not all word lengths; the infinite theorem depends on proof and classical free-group logspace word equality.

value.rationale: This assigns a precise deterministic logarithmic-space bound to a natural i-conjugacy-geodesic language that is known to lie outside CF and co-CF in rank at least two. The implicit-tree edge-parity method removes the apparent need to retain linear-sized trees and computes a natural entire-conjugacy-class exact length invariant. This is a motivated algorithmic gap rather than a finite-table computation.
